Here’s a short list of well‑known documentaries you might enjoy:

| Title | Release year | Synopsis |
|-------|--------------|----------|
| **“An Inconvenient Truth”** (2006) | Follows former U.S. Vice President Al Gore as he presents his climate change findings to an international audience. It sparked widespread public debate and won two Oscars. |
| **“An Inconvenient Sequel: Truth to Power”** (2017) | A follow‑up where Gore revisits the progress made since the first film and highlights new science and policy challenges. |
| **“Before the Flood”** (2019) | Leonardo DiCaprio travels around the world meeting scientists, activists, and leaders while exploring how human activity threatens our planet. |
| **“Climate Change – The Facts”** (2020) | An animated overview produced by the BBC that explains the science behind climate change and what it means for future generations. |
| **“Our Planet”** (2019) | While primarily focused on biodiversity, this Netflix series includes several episodes dedicated to climate impacts across ecosystems worldwide. |

If you'd prefer something more recent or regionally focused, let me know your preferences—such as length, format (film vs. mini-series), or whether you're looking for free streaming options—and I’ll tailor my recommendation further!
